blind_comparisons.question: Which per-frame damage-nulled series belongs to a roll a player could use reactively against a committed swing?
blind_comparisons.blind_rationale: B opens its invulnerable window 4 frames after input and holds it for 13 frames, so a roll started on the windup still covers the active frames. A opens at frame 9 and closes at 15, which only covers late-active frames and would be beaten by any early-active attack.

checks.observed: 50/50 overlapping swings produced a damage event; zero rng_calls in hit-resolution frames.
Roll input at recovery frames 2/5/10 did not truncate the attack's remaining recovery frames.

biggest_gap.what: The roll grants a median of 7 invulnerable frames, opening at roll frame 9; RI-CMB03 requires 13 +/-1 opening by frame 4. Measured over 120 scripted rolls at light load.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: A player who reads the windup correctly and rolls on time still takes the hit, so the fight never teaches its own timing.

remedy.action: Stop deriving invulnerability from the animation clip. Add an explicit i-frame window to the roll state: open at roll frame 4, close at frame 16 (13 frames inclusive) at light load, driven by the roll state machine and exposed in the trace as `invuln:true` so it is measurable.
remedy.acceptance: tools/harness/iframe-sweep.mjs over 120 rolls reports median 13 +/-1 invulnerable frames with first invulnerable frame index 4 +/-1, and zero damage events inside the window.

secondary_observations.what: Roll stamina cost is 0.42 of a light swing, below the 0.45 floor, so roll-spam is never punished within 5 rolls.
